headline: Prices offset the Mantoverde strike; profit swings positive

kpis.label: C1 cash cost (Cu, net of by-product credits)

summary_short: Revenue of $652.5M USD (+22.4% y/y) and record adjusted EBITDA of $329.1M (+82.9% y/y) as a $5.92/lb realized copper price offset an 11% drop in Q1 output caused by a 35-day strike at Mantoverde. 2026 production and cost guidance reaffirmed.
summary_long: Revenue rose 22.4% y/y to $652.5M on a $5.92/lb realized copper price (up from $4.36 y/y) despite an 11% drop in sulphide copper output driven by a 35-day strike at Mantoverde. Adjusted EBITDA of $329.1M was the sixth straight quarterly record. Net income swung to $102.5M ($0.13/share) from a $6.8M loss y/y. Consolidated C1 cash cost was $2.66/lb, up $0.07/lb y/y — lower volumes added $0.31/lb, partially offset by $0.25/lb of higher by-product credits. Balance sheet ended with $394.1M cash and $737.5M net debt (-$42.6M q/q). Mantoverde recoveries hit a record 90.3%. Full-year 2026 production and cost guidance unchanged.
confidence_notes: Capstone reports in USD; Yahoo-timeseries shard mislabels revenue/NI unit as CAD — the company's own USD figures are used in the summary. Adjusted EBITDA ($329.1M) differs from a mechanical Yahoo EBITDA on our shard ($311.9M) because the company excludes non-recurring items. AISC is not published — Capstone reports only C1. Y/Y net income delta is a swing from a small loss ($-6.8M → $102.5M), so a percentage is not meaningful and is shown as a swing. Full-year 2026 guidance ranges are unchanged (200-230kt Cu, C1 $2.45-2.75/lb, sustaining capex $270M, expansionary $225M, capitalized stripping $225M).

drivers.explanation: Higher realized copper prices ($5.92/lb vs $4.36 y/y) and stronger gold and silver by-product prices lifted revenue despite lower copper volumes.
Sixth straight quarter of record adjusted EBITDA, driven by higher realized copper prices and stronger gold and silver prices.

Sulphide output was 11% lower y/y, primarily driven by a 35-day strike at Mantoverde that reduced mill throughput and blocked access to higher-grade ore; Pinto Valley also had ~12 days of unplanned maintenance on the filter plant and concentrate storage.

drivers.metric: C1 cash cost (Cu, net of by-product credits)
drivers.explanation: Consolidated C1 rose $0.07/lb y/y: lower production volumes added $0.31/lb, partially offset by $0.25/lb of higher by-product credits from stronger gold and silver prices, particularly at Mantoverde and Cozamin.
Swing from a small loss driven by increased earnings from mining operations on higher realized copper prices.

Prices carried the quarter — realized copper $5.92/lb (up 36% y/y) plus record Mantoverde recoveries at 90.3% offset a strike-hit output quarter. Full-year 2026 production and cost guidance unchanged.
